memos.risk:
Risk officer call: **refuse the buy.**

The brief doesn't support a position. Price is 80% off its 30-minute high, return is -54% over 30 minutes, and the last 15 minutes show net selling (sells 21.4 SOL vs buys 18.9 SOL, 52 sellers vs 32 buyers). That's a coin in active distribution, not a dip with buyers stepping in.

Pool depth is 58 SOL, so a $20 ticket is about 0.1 SOL, and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is painful on top of a coin already falling. The launch bot, the 0.86 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes, and the 0.19 completer share add further reasons for caution.

If the desk ever revisits this, the conditions would be: net buy flow turning positive over several intervals, the sell-to-buy ratio falling well below 1, and a higher-low structure forming. Even then, I'd cap at $5, use a 20% stop, and hold no longer than 15 minutes. Right now, skip.
memos.scout:
Honest case for buying NOOB now: thin. The strongest points in the brief are that it's classed ORGANIC, not a factory or operator-backed coin, with no airdrop dump seen and a low bundle share (8.2%) and top-3 curve share (7.6%). The curve shows 244 buyers, and the graduation-window buying was broad (146 buyers ex-agent, top-5 buyer share 17.5%).

But demand is fading. The coin is down 54% over 30 minutes and 80% from its 30-minute high. In the last 15 minutes, sell SOL (21.4) exceeded buy SOL (18.9), with 52 sellers against 32 buyers, and the 2-minute post-graduation sell-to-buy ratio was 0.86. Pool depth is only 58 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces meaningful impact. Nothing here shows demand that will still be present in 30-60 minutes.

Verdict: no sufficient case to buy. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a slow bleed from the post-graduation exit wave, not a sudden rug. Price is already down 80% from its 30-minute high and 54% over 30 minutes, and the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (21.43) outrunning buy SOL (18.89), with 52 sellers against 32 buyers and net outflow of 2.53 SOL. The first two minutes after graduation were also sell-heavy (sell-to-buy ratio 0.86) with a launch bot present, which suggests early buyers are already distributing into the curve. Buying here means catching a falling knife with a pool of only 57.97 SOL, so a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is a large share of any bounce, and a coin in this state rarely recovers a dip. Organic classification and a low bundle share are not enough to offset the active selling pressure. Skip.
